title: Platform ops scrub and triage - 2026-11-25
content:
Meeting: Platform ops scrub + triage
Date: 2026-11-25 10:00-10:50 PT
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Diego Vasquez, Ethan Patel, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Julia (SRE on-call, joined 10:15)
Optional: Joel dropped a quick note re: dedicated capacity trial

Agenda:
- Quick rundowns: control plane / routing / auth / quotas (5m each)
- Bug scrub: prioritize faults from last 48h (KV cache, routing fallthrough)
- Quota policy rollback plan + impact analysis
- Action items and owners

Notes / quick statuses:
1) Control plane
- Recent rollout of allocator v2 (canary yesterday) shows small spike in RPC latencies for short-tail requests (~12-18ms p95 bump). Attribution: allocator rebalancing loop doing aggressive hot-shard moves.
- Diego ran heap / goroutine sampling; suspect lock contention in shard-assignment path (core pkg: allocator/assign.go).
- Mitigation: throttle reassignment frequency and add jitter. Patch in PR (github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/412) ready for test.
- Open ticket: PLTFM-987 (tracking allocator throttling + canary rollback criteria).
- Note: need to coordinate with Dedicated rollout schedule (>50% risk window during end-of-month customer loads).

2) Routing
- Observed ~0.3% increase in route misses when embedding model variants are used (route-selector seems to prefer v1 instead of v2 for multi-arch groups).
- Root cause likely metadata mismatch in metadata service (tags not propagated during model upload workflow).
- Temporary fix: force-route configuration for affected customers (customer tag: corp-fin). Ethan to push temporary route override via admin console.
- Longer fix: metadata-service will get a backfill job (see linear CPL-412).

3) Auth
- Rolling key rotation job for token-signing encountered a rate-limit from KMS region eu-west-2; some token issuances failed with retryable errors.
- Impact: transient 502s for auth-heavy internal endpoints (not customer-facing API).
- Priya engaged infra to bump KMS throughput and added per-AZ backoff.
- Question for security: do we need a fallback signing key (hot standby) for cross-region KMS issues? Action: Priya to draft proposal and cost estimate.

4) Quotas
- Quota enforcement change merged on Thursday to tighten burst windows for free-tier. After merge, we saw an increase in customer support tickets (~18%) for unexpected throttles.
- Root cause: default quota window decreased from 60s to 30s in config; rollback candidate prepared.
- Decision: rollback today for immediate relief, then ship a gradual enforcement plan with clearer telemetry.
- Action owner: Liam to coordinate rollback and create postmortem notes.

Incidents / recent issues to triage:
- Incident A (minor): KV cache degenerations on small sequence-length tails. Symptom: high lock contention in cache pruning path. Triage: Increase cache prune interval + add counters to observe flop rate. Diego/Julia to deploy experiment to canary nodes.
- Incident B (customer-impacting): Quota enforcement unexpected: several PLG users hit new burst limit and filed tickets. Support flagged high-latency workflows that now get throttled. Action: rollback, support playbook updated, CS notified.

Blocked items / questions:
- Can we get a simple feature flag toggle for allocator reassignment frequency? (Diego: yes, but needs a quick config model and safer defaults.)
- Is there appetite from security to allow hot-standby signing keys for emergency KMS outages? (Priya to set up meeting with SecOps next Tues.)
- Who owns the customer communication for quota rollback? (Liam + CS)

Action items (owner - ETA):
- Diego: push allocator reassignment throttle patch to staging and run 12h bake (ETA: 2026-11-26 EOD).
- Ethan: apply temporary force-route overrides for corp-fin accounts and document in admin-runbook (ETA: 2026-11-25 COB).
- Priya: write KMS fallback proposal and rough cost/risks (ETA: 2026-12-02).
- Liam: perform quota rollback, update support templates, publish customer notice draft (ETA: rollback complete by 2026-11-25 17:00 PT).
- Diego + Julia: deploy KV cache prune interval experiment to canary, collect metrics for 24h (ETA: start 2026-11-25 14:00 PT).
- Maya: schedule follow-up scrub next Wed 2026-12-02; include SRE on-call rotation review and dedicated-capacity risk assessment (ETA: calendar invite by EOD).

Decisions made:
- Immediate quota rollback to previous window (60s) approved to stop customer pain.
- Allocator throttle patch to be tested in staging; if metrics show <5% p95 increase, canary will continue otherwise rollback.

Back-of-envelope estimates / notes:
- Quota rollback expected to reduce support ticket rate by ~70% within 2 hours of rollout (based on last-day spike).
- Allocator fix should drop p95 back to baseline within 1-2 iterations after throttle deployed. Watch CPU on allocator pods.

Unresolved / follow-up questions:
- Need a canonical owner for quota policy changes (Product + Platform?) Suggestion: Product-hosted-api + eng-platform-engineering co-own.
- Instrumentation gaps: routing metadata propagation needs per-update counters so we can alert on tag-skew.

Misc / notes to self:
- Link to customer thread about quota throttles: thread-#support-1248 (Slack).
- Reminder: design doc for allocator v3 is in progress; add short compatibility section for rolling reassignments.

Next meeting: 2026-12-02 10:00 PT (platform ops scrub)

Raw scratchpad (things said off-record):
- "If we don't get better observable counters in metadata service, we'll chase symptoms forever." -- Ethan
- "I don't want signing fallback without a clear KMS security approval, but we should have an emergency runbook." -- Priya

End of notes.
